column1: # COMPOUNDING TEST: V09's VICReg terms + E3's schedule, on the Q02 base.
# User direction 2026-09-21 ("launch it in a similar setup as E3 too, to see how it could compound").
# WHY. Two independent gains over Q02 (0.3783) have been measured, from different mechanisms:
#   V09 = Q02 + VICReg var 1x + cov 10x (delta_z) -> 0.3846  (+0.0063)  F-vicreg1, 4/5
# X01 applies BOTH. If they are independent the naive expectation is ~0.3996; anything much
# below that means they overlap, and anything above means they interact positively.
# ⚠️ THE MECHANISMS ARE NOT OBVIOUSLY INDEPENDENT. F-ckpt3 showed the oscillation never settles
# (last-5-epoch swing 0.0381, largest consecutive jump 0.1744) and that the selector reliably
# catches peaks -- so part of E3's gain may be "more peaks sampled" rather than better
# convergence. VICReg's covariance term attacks representational redundancy (effective rank
# 33/512, F-latent7), which could plausibly make the trajectory less erratic and therefore
# reduce how much extra epochs buy. A sub-additive result would be evidence for exactly that.
# X02 is the 90-epoch variant, because if the gain is "more peaks sampled" it should keep
# growing with epochs, whereas a convergence gain should saturate.
# HELD FIXED: the Q02 loss (dcos 0.5, delta_mag 0.01363, latent MSE 0.0044) and V09's VICReg
# weights (var 0.0487, cov 0.0081, gamma 0.55, delta_z). Arm s313 otherwise, seed 42.
# `mae` is an ERROR: LOWER IS BETTER.
# PRE-REGISTERED. X01 ~ 0.3996 -> the two gains are independent and both mechanisms are real.
# X01 ~ 0.393 (i.e. no better than E3) -> VICReg's gain was the same thing the longer schedule
# already buys, and F-vicreg1's +0.0063 is not additive value. X01 > 0.400 -> positive
# interaction. X02 > X01 -> the epochs effect is still unsaturated even with VICReg on.
arm
